articles.title: Odisha Chief Engineer Throws Bundles of Cash from Flat During Vigilance Raid — ₹2.5 Crore Seized
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bhubaneswar, Odisha: In a dramatic turn of events, Vigilance officials raided seven locations linked to Baikunthanath Sarangi, Chief Engineer in Odisha’s Rural Development Department, just a day before his retirement. The raids led to the seizure of ₹2.51 crore in cash.

body.html:
Bhubaneswar, Odisha: In a dramatic turn of events, Vigilance officials raided seven locations linked to Baikunthanath Sarangi, Chief Engineer in Odisha’s Rural Development Department, just a day before his retirement. The raids led to the seizure of ₹2.51 crore in cash.

The operation took an unexpected twist when Sarangi, in a desperate move, allegedly threw bundles of ₹500 notes from his flat, apparently attempting to dispose of incriminating evidence. The cash was later recovered by officials.

Baikunthanath Sarangi is scheduled to retire on May 31. The raid and cash recovery have raised serious questions about corruption and misuse of office at senior levels of the state bureaucracy.

The Odisha Vigilance Department has confirmed the seizure and stated that further investigation is underway to trace the source and purpose of the massive cash haul.

body.html:
Himachal Pradesh: A landslide occurred near Shillai village in the Sirmaur district, triggering panic among travelers. A group of car riders narrowly escaped with their lives by jumping out and running away just in time.

The sudden landslide sent rocks and debris crashing down the hillside, barely missing the vehicle. Fortunately, no injuries were reported.

The incident highlights the ongoing risk of landslides in the region during the pre-monsoon season. Authorities have urged travelers to exercise caution on hilly routes.

articles.title: Bareilly: Man Mocked Over Marriage Climbs Roof, Rescued After 5-Hour Police Operation
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: In a dramatic incident from Sirauli, Bareilly, a 25-year-old man named Gurudev was rescued by police on Wednesday, May 28, after he climbed onto the roof of a two-storey house, threatening to take his own life.

body.html:
In a dramatic incident from Sirauli, Bareilly, a 25-year-old man named Gurudev was rescued by police on Wednesday, May 28, after he climbed onto the roof of a two-storey house, threatening to take his own life.

Gurudev, who got married just over a month ago, had reportedly been facing relentless mockery and humiliation from villagers and even relatives. Many questioned how he could have married someone with a “model-like figure” and a “Miss Universe-like attitude,” repeatedly labelling him “mad.”

What began as light teasing escalated into deeply hurtful remarks, pushing Gurudev into mental distress. "They kept saying things like, ‘How did you manage to marry such a girl?’ It became character assassination," a local villager told Dainik Bhaskar.

Police were alerted around 4 PM on May 28. Officers from Sirauli Police Station, led by SHO Ram Ratan Singh, along with SI Ramveer Singh and constables Shubham Kumar and Manoj Kumar, rushed to the scene. A safety setup including tarpaulins, nets, and mattresses was arranged, and both police and locals pleaded with Gurudev to come down.

After nearly five hours of effort, the police successfully brought Gurudev down safely. The Bareilly Police later shared details of the operation on social media, praising the coordinated effort between the police and the public.
